title: בר קפרא

paragraphs: Bar Kappara. His name was Shimon: end of Hagigah. (Mattenot Kehunah, Kohelet, on ‘What advantage has a man,’ wrote that his name was Abba; he erred.) He composed the Mishnah of bar Kappara (in Ra'avad's received account: he wrote the Tosefta). He and Hizkiyah were tannaim and older than R' Yehudah Nesia (see there). At the end of Ha-Ro'eh, 63a, bar Kappara expounded: ‘When things are cheap, gather and buy; where there is no man, there be a man.’ Abaye said, ‘Learn from this: where there is a man, do not be a man.’ It is difficult: why does Abaye not draw this inference from the Mishnah in Avot, ‘In a place where there are no men, strive to be a man,’ and say, ‘Abaye said: learn from this,’ etc.? As for bar Kappara, one need not ask what he teaches us, since it is a Mishnah, because bar Kappara is a tanna (שנ״ח [work unidentified], Metzora). His place was Parvad: Rashi, Avodah Zarah 31a. R' Shimon son of Rabbi and bar Kappara sat studying, and a teaching was difficult for them. R' Shimon son of Rabbi said, ‘This matter requires Rabbi.’ Bar Kappara told him, ‘What can Rabbi say about this?’ R' Shimon son of Rabbi went and told his father, who took offense. When bar Kappara came to visit Rabbi, Rabbi told him, ‘I do not recognize you,’ hinting that he did not wish to see him. Bar Kappara observed the restrictions of rebuke for thirty days: Mo'ed Katan 16, end of a. R' Hiyya swore that this was what he had heard from Rabbi, and bar Kappara swore that this was what he had heard from Rabbi: Yevamot 32b. Rabbi asked bar Kappara, ‘What does it imply?’ Pesahim 42a. He caused Rabbi to dance at the wedding of Rabbi's son Shimon: Nedarim 51a. In Kiddushin 33a:7, Bar Kappara took offense because R' Shimon son of Rabbi did not rise before him [another reading names R' Shmuel son of R' Yosi instead of Bar Kappara]. He used to sell sayings for dinars: end of Berakhot. He became angry at his two pupils, and they did not live out their year: Berakhot 39a; also Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot chapter 6, Mishnah 2. When Rabbi died, they sent him to see whether Rabbi was dead (see above, R' Yehudah Ha-Nasi). He used to mock ben Elasa, and Rabbi cursed him (see there). R' Hoshaya bar Hama bar Bisna was his pupil. ‘R' Elazar said in bar Kappara's name: R' Meir used to say’: Yoma 46a:2 [Heilprin reads א״ר לאלעזר]. Rav Huna in bar Kappara's name: Bereshit Rabbah, Lekh Lekha, chapter 46, Avraham expounded, ‘Orlah is said of a tree,’ etc. This exposition in Kedoshim, chapter 25, has ‘Rav Huna said: bar Kappara’; it is a scribal error and should read ‘in bar Kappara's name.’ Yuhasin, under het: R' Hiyya bar Abba, or bar Adda, was his sister's son. This is a scribal error; rather, bar Pada was his sister's son (see there). See R' Yehudah ben Pedaya, bar Kappara's sister's son. R' Hama bar Bisna disagrees with him. R' Hanina bar Hama in his name. R' Yehoshua ben Levi in his name: Ta'anit 26, end of b; Sukkah 38b; Hullin 45, end of a, 98a. See R' Shimon ben Pazi: R' Yehoshua ben Levi said much in bar Kappara's name. R' Yohanan was his pupil. R' Yonah in his name. R' Yosi ben Patros. In R' Yirmeyah ben Elazar's name (see there): I have not found this. He asked R' Yishmael bar R' Yosi. ‘R' Meir used to say’ (see above). Bar Pada, his sister's son: see above and there. He spoke to R' Pedaya. Also Rav, R' Hanina, R' Yonatan, and R' Yehoshua ben Levi: Jerusalem Talmud, Megillah 1:7. Also רבב״ח [name unresolved]. R' Shimon ben Pazi in his name. Resh Lakish in his name. R' Tanhum of Parvad was his pupil. R' Tanhum said: bar Kappara expounded two expositions in Sepphoris; Helek, 93b, 94a.
